title: Antiferromagnetic pseudospintronics without spin splitting
authors: Shu-Hui Zhang, Shu-Qi Liu, Dan-Yang Han, Zhan Kong, Ding-Fu Shao, Wen Yang, Kai Chang
abstract: Antiferromagnets (AFMs) are promising for high-density spintronics due to their zero net magnetization, yet conventional AFM spintronics relies on spin splitting-a requirement that excludes many collinear AFMs with compensated spin sublattices. Here we exploit the sublattice degree of freedom in a honeycomb AFM with zero spin splitting. We uncover a coupling between spin and sublattice: the out-of-plane pseudospin polarization is spin-dependent, a mechanism we term partial pseudospin-spin coupling. This allows switching of the pseudospin polarization by reversing the Néel vector. Introducing an impurity into a specific sublattice induces Friedel oscillations with a sublattice-resolved amplitude ratio dictated solely by the pseudospin polarization, which is directly measurable by spin-polarized scanning tunneling microscopy. Furthermore, we demonstrate Néel-vector-controlled transmission and a large nonvolatile tunneling magnetoresistance in an all-in-one AFM junction, with pronounced resonant enhancement in gate-tunable two-dimensional devices. Our work establishes a new paradigm-AFM pseudospintronics-that utilizes the sublattice pseudospin in zero-spin-splitting AFMs, extending spintronics beyond the conventional spin-splitting paradigm.
summary: This work pioneers AFM pseudospintronics by utilizing the sublattice degree of freedom in antiferromagnets that lack conventional spin splitting. The key mechanism identified is a partial pseudospin–spin coupling, which allows for switching polarization by reversing the Néel vector. This leads to measurable effects like NV-controlled tunneling and large nonvolatile magnetoresistance.
main_problem: To develop a new paradigm for spintronics, termed AFM pseudospintronics, that operates in antiferromagnets (AFMs) without relying on the conventional requirement of spin splitting.
main_result: The study demonstrates that sublattice degrees of freedom can be exploited via partial pseudospin–spin coupling to achieve Néel-vector-controlled transmission and a large nonvolatile pseudomagnetoresistance effect.
method: Theoretical analysis involving tight-binding models, Fourier transforms applied to Friedel oscillations (FOs), and calculation of tunneling magnetoresistance ratios.
model_or_system: The system is a honeycomb AFM modeled by a tight-binding Hamiltonian incorporating sublattice pseudospin ($\hat{	au}$) and real spin ($\hat{\sigma}$). The physics hinges on the coupling between these degrees of freedom in zero spin-splitting collinear AFMs.
key_observables: Sublattice-resolved Friedel oscillation amplitude ratio ($R_s$), Néel vector (NV)-controlled transmission, and nonvolatile pseudomagnetoresistance (PMR).
important_parameters: Pseudospin polarization ($ ar{\sigma}_z^s = \Lambda_s/\epsilon$), doping level ($\epsilon$), and junction potential ($V_0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes interfaces are along zigzag directions to simplify scattering processes, allowing the conservation of spin and valley in tunneling calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spin-degenerate band structure and pseudospin polarization; they show sublattice-resolved FOs (intravalley/intervalley) used to extract the ratio $R$; and finally, they depict the NV control over junction transmission and PMR magnitude.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework by introducing the Hamiltonian and the concept of partial pseudospin–spin coupling. It then derives measurable quantities like the amplitude ratio from FOs, demonstrating local probing of the NV state. Finally, it applies this understanding to predict large nonvolatile PMR effects in junctions.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the use of symmetry breaking (NV reversal) to control electronic transport properties via internal degrees of freedom (sublattice pseudospin) is relevant to open quantum systems where multiple coupled order parameters govern dynamics.
